    You are the construction manager

    Build a data center campus, one phase at a time

    Created by Ali Keyvanfar, Ph.D.

    Red Clay Ridge is a made-up site of about 45 acres off a county road in Georgia, next to a street of homes. A company wants a data center campus there. Your job is to build it in the right order, keep the schedule, the budget and the crew safe, and work with the neighbors. The game shows facts and trade-offs. It does not take a side on data centers.

    Pick a phase, place each of its key elements, then finish the phase. Issue cards will interrupt you. Your choices move the dashboard and the neighborhood panel.

    Keys: Tab moves between buttons · Enter or Space presses · N = next step · M = effects on the map on/off · V = voice on/off · on the 3D view, arrow keys turn and + or − zoom. The game asks you to decide when each choice matters.

    Issue card

    Choose one

    Turnover: the campus is handed to its owner

    The building is now an operating facility. Construction jobs wind down and a smaller operations staff takes over. Every choice you made traded time, money, safety or neighbor effects. Different communities weigh these trade-offs differently.

      Still building?

      Build the Campus

      Created by Ali Keyvanfar, Ph.D.

      A personal public-education project, drawing on construction research at Kennesaw State University. Made-up site and companies; durations are typical ranges and vary by project.

      A companion to Community Builders of Pecan Grove.

      How this is scored. Neighbor relations counts truck traffic, construction noise and dust. Jobs, taxes, power and water are shown on their own rows, because they are not the same kind of effect. Schedule, budget and safety add up your decisions and the issue cards. The words run from Concern to Strong. Cooling changes power use and water use on the panel; it is not a point for or against the project.

      Kiosk setup: on a library computer, download this page and open the file in a full-screen browser. It works with no network. Opened from the web, the page also saves a copy so a later reload can work offline.

      Narration uses an AI text-to-speech service (a stock voice). three.js r170 (MIT). Geist and Inter fonts (SIL Open Font License).
